newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Death toll rises to 23 in Central African fighting.
newsitem.headline: Death toll rises to 23 in Central African fighting.

text.p: The death toll in fighting between disaffected soldiers and peacekeepers in Bangui, the capital of the Central African Republic, has risen to 23, officials of the Central African Red Cross said on Sunday.
Around 70 people have been wounded in the fighting which began on Friday.
They include five French nationals, who were hit on Saturday by two stray mortar bombs that fell on the French embassy compound. Further details on the dead and wounded were not available.
Witnesses reported an uneasy calm in the capital on Sunday morning, with just the occasional burst of automatic fire being heard. The streets were deserted.
The African peacekeeping force has been deployed since a January 25 peace deal that ended a series of mutinies.

That deal, brokered by Mali's respected former military leader Amadou Toumani Toure included a plan to reintegrate the mutineers from the paramilitary gendarmerie into their units, but efforts to achieve this have failed.
Toure was due to arrive in Bangui on Sunday afternoon in an attempt to intercede again.

Mutinies in April and May 1996 began as protests over pay but became a movement to topple President Ange-Felix Patasse, a northern civilian elected in 1993. The third mutiny began in November and degenerated into ethnic bloodshed.

French troops, in the country under a defence pact, restored order after the last mutiny and then handed over to the peacekeepers. The African force includes soldiers from Burkina Faso, Chad, Gabon, Mali, Senegal and Togo.
